gen-gf-gabarito-gf-stick: Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, its terminals cut open so every counter flows outward into the margin. Stick follows in tubelike lines of constant weight, and paragraphs of it stay light and passable.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-suse: Approachable curves in SUSE open into bowls like a ladle tipped toward you, while Gabarito up top keeps its nib-drawn, outward-flowing terminals. Expressive display above, friendly sans below: that mix is the whole charm.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-suse-mono: SUSE Mono reads with open curves and extra room on both sides of each letter, so nothing crowds. And Gabarito, with its constant stroke and no sparkle, leads into paragraphs that would stay easy to move through.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tajawal: Distinctive from the first line, Gabarito holds one stroke width throughout. Tajawal does its best work lower down, where its c becomes a broad open hook and a sans body can simply carry the words.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tasa-explorer: Gabarito draws with the constant weight of a stencil-cut channel, its terminals opened so the counters flow outward. TASA Explorer handles the reading, with curves that end like brush strokes lifted early, a softer job than the heading's bold gesture.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tasa-orbiter: Loud channel lines, then quiet detail. Gabarito's outline can be traced with a finger, while TASA Orbiter keeps every small counter unclogged, so a long sans paragraph stays crisp and clear.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-teachers: Contemporary in feel, this pairing sets Gabarito's nib-drawn heading, terminals cut open, over something far lighter. Teachers bends thin steel-rod letters whose ink strokes taper out before touching, and that fine-versus-bold gap is the strongest thing here.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-telex: Zero modulation in the line is what defines Gabarito, a heading with open terminals and nothing swelling or thinning. And Telex, a plain sans with curvy, unclamped letters, takes over the quiet reading work.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tenor-sans: Tenor Sans keeps its c tips from creeping toward touching, with a slight tug of heavier verticals against lighter horizontals. But Gabarito above draws one plotter-pen weight, so the two feel clearly different on the page.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tirra: Gabarito runs its strokes like thread stitched along a path, with terminals cut open and counters flowing outward. And Tirra, a sans-serif with round forms like open parentheses, gives the pair its strongest quality: a lively heading over a gentle body.
